'''All Decked Out''' is [[Richard Handley|Rich Handley]]'s report in ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' #48 (April 2000, pages 78–79) on the [[1999 Decipher World Championship]] at [[DecipherCon 1999]].<ref name="swi48" /><ref name="wook-48" /> Its subtitle is "The Competition is Fierce at Decipher's 4th Annual Star Wars CCG World Championships". The contents page lists it as "Decipher This!".<ref name="swi48" />

[[File:Star Wars Insider 48 page 78.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Star Wars Insider #48, page 78.]]
[[File:Star Wars Insider 48 page 79.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Star Wars Insider #48, page 79.]]

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==
Thirty-two finalists met at the Cavalier Hotel in Virginia Beach, Virginia, on 11–14 November 1999. Reigning champion [[Matt Potter]] of Minnesota was among them. Most had qualified at local events. The last two seats went to an eight-hour Wild Card Open on Thursday.<ref name="swi48" />

Day One on Friday cut the field to 12 players. On Saturday the 12 played until two were left: [[Gary Carman]] of Bristol, England, and [[Steven Lewis]] of Nashville, Tennessee. Attendees watched their final on a video feed in an adjoining room.<ref name="swi48" />

Carman won and became the 1999 Star Wars CCG World Champion. [[Kyle Heuer]] said it was the third time a British player had reached the final, and the first British win.<ref name="swi48" /> [[Mark Tuttle]], Decipher's Star Wars Discussion List moderator, said: "Both players played masterfully."<ref name="swi48" />

Carman won the first game with 28 minutes and 47 seconds on the clock. In Game Two he faced Lewis's hidden base. His plan was to drain at [[Kiffex]] and [[Kessel]]. Lewis won Game Two with five minutes and 44 seconds left. Carman's 22-card lead from the first game still gave him the title.<ref name="swi48" />

The magazine prints the third-place name as "Martin Akessan".<ref name="swi48" />

== Other events ==
Players outside the title race played [[DecipherCon 1999 Allegiances|Allegiances]], [[DecipherCon 1999 No Such Thing As Luck|No Such Thing As Luck]] and the [[DecipherCon 1999 Iron Man|Iron Man]]. Several Sealed Deck formats ran as well, some with Japanese decks. Players rated 1800 or more on 8 November could enter the [[DecipherCon 1999 Invitational|Star Wars Invitational]].<ref name="swi48" />

The convention also held the first [[Young Jedi]] CCG World Championship. [[Jonathan Quesenberry]] said: "Young Jedi is a much quicker game than Star Wars."<ref name="swi48" /> [[Greg Heisler]] of St. Louis won with a Dark Side deck full of tanks. He had come to qualify for the Star Wars Open, lost, and entered Young Jedi instead. [[Matthew Reed]] placed second.<ref name="swi48" />

== Guests and announcements ==
[[Jeremy Bulloch]], Boba Fett in the films, signed photographs of himself as Boba Fett. "It's a real pleasure to be here," he said.<ref name="swi48" /> [[Shannon Baksa]], cast by Decipher as Mara Jade, also signed photographs. She wore the leather-and-cape costume from her card and carried a replica of Mara's lightsaber.<ref name="swi48" />

Decipher displayed upcoming cards, including a computer-generated Dengar and a modified Z-95 Headhunter. [[Warren Holland]] announced that [[Death Star II]] would be the last era-specific expansion for the time being. Later sets would focus on single characters, starting with [[Luke Skywalker]] and [[Darth Vader]].<ref name="swi48" />

== Player cards ==
The article prints its winners as Star Wars CCG cards. Rich Handley took the photographs. Game text and stats as printed:<ref name="swi48" />

* [[Gary Carman]]: Power 4, Ability 3. "Deploys in Bristol, England, with laser focus, cunning strategy, and strong Force powers. Wins the Star Wars CCG World Championship."
* [[Steven Lewis]]: Power 4, Ability 3. "Deploys in Tennessee and wherever in the universe there's a good CCG game brewing. Places 2nd in Star Wars."
* [[Greg Heisler]]: Used Interrupt. "Deploys in St. Louis at +4 power. Force is strong in this one. Wins Young Jedi World Championship."
* [[Matthew Reed]]: Power 4, Ability 3. "Deploys with both fierce competition and the meditative calm of a Jedi. Places 2nd in Young Jedi."
* Site card: "Shannon Baksa (Mara Jade) and Jeremy Bulloch (Boba Fett) sign autographs for fans during breaks in the action."
